[b]Lungs of Steel 2, Molten Fury[/b]

[i]The new hit film from the Great West has hit the eastern lands yet yearning for the latest action flick. This marks the second film in an increasingly popular series that takes place in the Planet of Dirt, an alternate universe with its own lore and political system. Continuing where they left off in the last series, Fuhrer Ernst Röhm, put into as an allied puppet government after he led a secret faction within the National Socialist regime to betray Fuhrer Grok in the last movie, was contacted by his top scientist, the crazed and mad Werner Heisenberg, on the completion of his latest invention, the fruit of the Dresden Project, hinted in the last movie. Now, Ernest Röhm processes a device capable of ensuring that the new restored German Kingdom will not be a mere puppet of Imperica Brittancia and her allied democracies, a device capable of melting entire cities by heating everything with gamma rays.

Meanwhile, John Freedom, our protagonist in the last movie, struggles from the trauma of loosing his best friend, Joan Baguette, all whilst trying to take care of his wife, Scarlet Johansson, and his three beautiful children. He is then contacted by his old commander, General Eyepatch, for a top secret mission from a new security agency known as the Central Intelligence Organization. An old German agent and previous love interest named Frau Heißeskraut has been suspected of being in the capital of Brittancia, fishchips, with the goal of sabotaging the Empire by enacting a devastating horror attack with the Dresden Project. Thus, an old soldier must now become an expert spy, navigating both old love and new enemies as he seeks to stop the plan to obliterate the center of the Anglogram world.[/i]

[i]The film marks another successful project by vaunted film director and producer Al-Sahrrir and his increasingly powerful global media empire. While originally relegating himself to ordinary newspapers and broadcasters, his film successes show his organizational management skills really do stand out in the competitive environment of film production, managing to recruit notable stars like Vespurian Bron Blacker reprising his role as John Freedom, as well as Neue Republik actors Virhar Gehring as Ernst Röhm and Nora Siebert as Frau Heißeskraut. Al-Sahrrir even making a humorous camo for himself as a minor character and bartender. Bron Blacker has been especially praised, breaking himself out of a deadlock of neverending retinue comedy action films that he did alongside punching bag Barry Wilsonington and flexing some serious firepower in a true action roll. Virhar Gehring pendant for chewing out the scenery was notably praised in his performance as the eccentric leader of new Germany, and Nora Siebert remains hot. The successful challenge by Al-Sahrrir's more controversial directing style and more heavy rather than family friendly themes is sure to put pressure on traditional film studios to engage with more modern audience tastes.[/i]

[i]Lungs of Steel 2, Molten Fury is expected to make at least 1 dollar more than production and advertising expenses, but likely billions even. [/i]
